page.layout: One page of text, with a running head and page number at top; verse lines in the centre; handwritten annotations and a bracket in the margins (left and right), which are not printed text and are not transcribed as notes.

main_text.head: Senum pedes.
main_text.p:
Ferre pedes senio si languida membra recusant:
Et te nutantem terre recusat humus,
Euehitor fidei pennis: sic incola terrae
Dum fieri cessas, incipis esse poli.
main_text.head: Perfecutione crescit Ecclesia.
main_text.p:
Latior herba venit, ferro quae falcis acutę
Tondetur, prati sic geminatur honor.
Sic quos ense fero sequitúrque petitque tyrannus,
Christiadas, penitus quos periisse cupit:
Hoc magis augentur, numero, pietate, fideque:
Quo magè vultrillos trux abolere furor.
main_text.head: Adorare quid sit. ex Plinio in praef. lib. 32.
main_text.p:
Numen adorandum curuato corpore monstrat
Cultor arans, quando curuus adorat humum.
Pendentes propria cernas vt ab arbore fructus,
Attentus coelos vt tueare decet.
Quos tellus fundit fructus, Pomona Ceresve
Non dant, aut falso nomine reque Dij:
Quod prudens natura docet: largitur at illa
Solus adorandus, corpore, mente, Deus.

Votum Apollonij apud Philostratum. Nosse bonos
à bonis nosci, ignorare malos,
& ignorari à malis.

Nosse bonos, noscíque bonis, non vltima laus est:
Quam confueuerunt commoda multa sequi.
Nosse malos, noscíque malis, res proxima damnis
Nec non aerumnis innumerabilibus.

page.notes: Handwritten marginal annotations (Greek-looking marks, "Vide §. 161", "Nota") and a bracket at the right margin are manuscript additions and are omitted. Some words are faint or show-through; readings such as "Ceresve", "Quo magè vultrillos" and "aerumnis" are doubtful. Greek word in the Apollonius line is handwritten and not transcribed.
